samples.summary: Google strategy registration is decided at module-import time, before ConfigModule loads `.env` — a `.env`-configured deployment advertises Google but 500s on `/auth/google`
samples.evidence: `const googleProviders = googleAuthConfigured() ? [GoogleStrategy] : [];` (auth.module.ts:37) runs when the module file is *evaluated*, which is before the `@Module({ imports: [ConfigModule.forRoot(), ...] })` decorator below it (and before AppModule's `ConfigModule.forRoot({isGlobal:true})`, since app.module.ts imports auth.module.ts first). `oauth-providers.ts` reads `process.env` only. The backend's documented configuration mechanism is a `.env` file in the package (packages/backend/README.md:18 'Create a `.env` file in this package'), and `nest start` does not preload dotenv (packages/backend/package.json scripts have no `-r dotenv/config`). So with GOOGLE_* set only in `.env`, `googleAuthConfigured()` is false at line 37 and `GoogleStrategy` is never provided — yet `AuthController.authProviders()` (auth.controller.ts:240) and `assertGoogleConfigured()` (google-auth.guard.ts) evaluate the same function *per request*, after ConfigModule populated `process.env`, so both report/allow Google. Result: the login page shows the Google button, the guard lets the request through, and `AuthGuard('google')` fails with passport's `Unknown authentication strategy "google"` → 500 on every Google sign-in attempt. The half-configured boot warning also never fires, because all three vars *are* set at that later point.

samples.summary: `emailIsVerified` validates a verification flag that may belong to a different address than the email actually used
samples.evidence: `validate` picks `email = profile.emails?.[0]?.value ?? profile._json?.email` (line 73), but `emailIsVerified` accepts when *either* `profile.emails[0].verified === true` **or** `profile._json.email_verified === true` (lines 23-26). The two signals are not tied to the same address: if a profile ever carries an `emails[0]` distinct from `_json.email`, an unverified `emails[0]` is accepted on the strength of `_json.email_verified`, and since `findOrCreateUser` matches on email alone (user.service.ts:41-45) that signs the holder into whatever account owns the unverified address. The verification check should be evaluated against the address that is actually used.

samples.summary: Strict `=== true` on `email_verified` refuses the sign-in if Google returns the claim as a string
samples.evidence: `profile.emails?.[0]?.verified === true || profile._json?.email_verified === true`. Google's userinfo has historically returned `email_verified`/`verified_email` as the string `"true"` in some response shapes, and `passport-google-oauth20` copies the raw JSON value onto `emails[].verified` without coercion. A string value makes both comparisons false and every Google login is refused with `UnauthorizedException('Google account email is not verified')` — the feature fails closed for all users, with no way for the operator to fix it.

samples.summary: A Google profile with no/unverified email throws a 401 out of the guard instead of redirecting to the login page with `?error=`
samples.evidence: `validate` throws `UnauthorizedException` (lines 78 and 82). That is raised inside `GoogleCallbackGuard`/passport, so the visitor lands on raw backend JSON on the backend origin, with no way back — the exact failure mode the GitHub callback deliberately avoids (auth.controller.ts:143-150 explains the refusal is a redirect 'not a thrown 400' because backend JSON 'leaves the user staring at JSON with no way back'). The new provider's most likely user-facing failure takes the path the existing code argues against.

samples.summary: Google callback leaves the OAuth state cookie in place when it refuses a missing or non-web `state`
samples.evidence: The refusal condition short-circuits: `typeof stateToken !== 'string' || !isWebOAuthState(stateToken) || !consumeWebOAuthState(req, res, stateToken)`. When the first two disjuncts fire, `consumeWebOAuthState` — the only thing that clears `oauthStateCookieName()` — never runs, so the 10-minute state cookie survives a refused callback. `web-oauth-login.ts:60` documents the intended invariant ('The cookie is cleared whether or not it matches, so a failed login leaves nothing behind to replay'), and this path breaks it.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as the finding describes. google.strategy.ts:73 selects the address with `profile.emails?.[0]?.value ?? profile._json?.email`, while emailIsVerified (google.strategy.ts:22-27) accepts on EITHER `emails[0].verified === true` OR `_json.email_verified === true` — the verification signal is not bound to the address actually returned. Downstream there is no second check: auth.controller.ts:280-291 passes googleUser.email directly to UserService.findOrCreateUser, which matches on email alone (user.service.ts:41-45) and returns the pre-existing account, so accepting an unverified address means entering whatever account owns it. Refuting would require proving the two signals can never describe different addresses, i.e. that passport-google-oauth20@2.0.0 builds emails[0] from _json.email/_json.email_verified. I could not establish that from this repository: node_modules is absent (no matches for **/passport-google-oauth20/**), the constructor (google.strategy.ts:44-53) sets no userProfileURL so the parse path is implicit, and the only in-repo support for the coupling is a prose comment (google.strategy.ts:13-15) and a hand-written fixture (google.strategy.spec.ts:25-37) authored with the change — neither is independent evidence, and no test covers a profile where emails[0].value differs from _json.email. With the mechanism unverifiable in-tree and the failure mode being entry into another user's account, I cannot name a refutation ground. My suspicion is that the library ties both fields to the same claim, making this defensive rather than reachable, but that is external recollection, not repository fact, so the finding stands.

The finding turns entirely on whether the claim can arrive as the string "true"; I could not settle that from this repository because node_modules is absent (passport-google-oauth20 is only declared at packages/backend/package.json:64), so I could not read the library's profile parser or the @types declaration.
